topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, lecturer, and key learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: intrinsic mutations, environmental factors, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the fundamental causes of cancer, comparing intrinsic genetic and microenvironmental factors with environmental exposures and epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how infectious pathogens drive cancer development, using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the molecular mechanisms by which specific physical and chemical mutagens cause DNA damage, often through xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, host susceptibility, and carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how non-mutagenic tumour promoters, developmental stages, and host physiological factors cooperate with initial DNA damage to drive carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the analytical, experimental, and epidemiological methodologies used to detect carcinogenicity and evaluate cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing remarks and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding summary and wraps up the lecture.
